This vignette explains how RESY matches the species names of vegetation plots
to the species of an expert system. An expert system names species in its
species groups and rules; a plot record counts for such a species when it
refers to the same taxon or to a taxon within it. RESY decides this with a
**taxonomic backbone**: a reference list of taxon concepts with their synonyms
and their place in the taxonomic hierarchy. The expert systems bundled with
RESY use [EuroSL](https://eurosl.infinitenature.org), the European species
list built on Euro+Med PlantBase.

Plant names are ambiguous: the same name can stand for taxa of different
extent, and one taxon can have many names (Jansen & Dengler
[2010](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1654-1103.2010.01209.x)). Matching names as
character strings, or through tables of synonyms, therefore either misses
records or merges taxa that differ. Matching along a backbone keeps taxon
concepts apart.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(RESY)
```

## The backbone of an expert system

Section 1 of an expert system declares its backbone, with the name, the
address and the version of the list:

```{r section-1}
eunis <- resy_load_expert(scheme = "EUNIS")
eunis$backbone
```

In an expert file this is

```
SECTION 1: Taxonomic backbone
EuroSL https://eurosl.infinitenature.org 2026-11-24
SECTION 1: End
```

or, in a JSON expert file, a `backbone` object with the same three fields.
The published EUNIS-ESy releases (versions `2020-06-08`, `2021-06-01`,
`2025-10-03`) list species aggregations in Section 1 instead; see
[Older expert systems](#older-expert-systems) below.

RESY reads the backbone with the
[vegdata](https://cran.r-project.org/package=vegdata) package. Install EuroSL
once with

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
vegdata::taxref_download_eurosl()
```

and RESY finds it by itself. A list in another place is named with
`options(resy.backbone = <path>)`, either an SQLite file or a CSV file.
This vignette uses the part of EuroSL that ships with RESY and covers the
example data:

```{r backbone}
options(resy.backbone = system.file("extdata", "eurosl_example.csv.xz",
                                    package = "RESY"))
```

`resy_backbone()` returns the list itself:

```{r backbone-list}
bb <- resy_backbone(eunis)
nrow(bb)
head(bb[, c("TaxonName", "SYNONYM", "taxonRank", "TaxonConceptID")])
```

## How names are matched

`resy_check_taxonomy()` matches the names of a species table and reports, for
each name, how it was matched and which expert taxon it counts for. The
following names show the cases:

```{r examples}
names <- data.frame(TaxonName = c(
  "Fagus sylvatica L.",       # with author citation
  "Fagus sylvatca",           # spelling variant
  "Abies pectinata",          # synonym
  "Festuca rubra agg.",       # an aggregate
  "Quercus cf. robur",        # uncertain determination
  "Quercus sp.",              # genus only, EUNIS names the genus
  "Planta inventa"            # not in the backbone
))
checked <- resy_check_taxonomy(names, eunis)
checked[, c("scientificName", "TaxonName", "backbone_name", "match", "status")]
```

RESY uses the matching of vegdata (`vegdata::taxname.match()`), restricted to
steps that keep the taxon concept:

| Name in the data | Matched? |
|---|---|
| with an author citation, e.g. `Fagus sylvatica L.` | yes, the author is removed |
| a spelling variant, e.g. `Fagus sylvatca` | yes, if the backbone has a close name of the same genus whose epithet starts with the same three letters |
| a synonym, e.g. `Abies pectinata` | yes, to the accepted taxon |
| an aggregate, `agg.`, `aggr.`, `s. l.` | only to an aggregate (or section) of the backbone, never to the species of the same name |
| `s. str.` | no: whether it means the species of the backbone is left to you |
| a misapplied name (`auct.`) | no: it does not name the concept of the plain name |
| an uncertain determination (`cf.`, `aff.`, `?`) | no: what it represents is unknown, so it is ignored |

## Which expert taxon a plot taxon counts for

A plot taxon counts for an expert taxon when the backbone places it at or below
that taxon: a synonym counts for its accepted taxon, a subspecies for its
species, a species for its aggregate, and a species for its genus where the
expert system names a genus. When the expert system names several taxa above
a plot taxon, for example a species and its aggregate, the plot taxon counts
as the closest one, and a species group that holds the aggregate also counts
the species. Each plot record therefore counts once in each species group.

A record of a broader taxon does not count for a narrower expert taxon: a plot
record of `Festuca ovina agg.` says nothing about `Festuca ovina` in the narrow
sense.

The classification of the example plots shows the matching in
`res$taxon_resolution`:

```{r classify, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
species <- utils::read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "data_example_species.csv", package = "RESY")
)
header <- data.frame(PlotObservationID = unique(species$PlotObservationID))
res <- resy_classify(species, header, expert = eunis, mc = 1L)
head(res$taxon_resolution[, c("scientificName", "TaxonName", "status")])
```

## Names that cannot be used

`summary()` lists the names that do not count for any expert taxon although
they might, in two parts:

```{r summary}
summary(res$taxon_resolution)
```

**Potentially important** names may change a classification:

- `not found` with a genus the expert system uses: check the spelling, or
  whether the taxon is in the backbone under another name.
- `broader than expert taxon`: the record is of a taxon broader than the one
  the expert system names; determine it more precisely if possible.
- `expert taxon not in backbone`: the expert system names a taxon that the
  backbone lacks (for example an aggregate it does not distinguish), so the
  records of this species cannot count for it. This is for the authors of the
  expert system and of the backbone to resolve.
- `level unclear`: an aggregate or `s. str.` name that the backbone cannot
  place.

**Probably unimportant** names cannot affect the rules: records determined
only to genus or a higher rank, uncertain determinations, and names of genera
the expert system does not use.

Names the backbone knows but the expert system does not use (`not_used`) are
no problem: like all records, they count for the total cover and the number of
species of a plot.

## Older expert systems

The published EUNIS-ESy releases list species aggregations in Section 1: each
aggregate name with the names it includes. For these expert systems the names
in the plot data must be written as in the expert system; RESY merges the
names each aggregation lists and classifies them as they are.

```{r old-release, eval = FALSE}
res_2025 <- resy_classify(species, header, scheme = "EUNIS",
                          version = "2025-10-03")
```

The synonym table that RESY used to bridge other name sources to these
releases (`resy_resolve_taxa()`, `resy_read_synonyms()`,
`resy_canonical_species()`) is deprecated and will be removed in RESY 0.4.
